summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The market slipped on the latest day and its mood stays stressed with the trend down. All five calls stay neutral with low conviction. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: The runners slowed a little again, and the race is still bumpy. The brain still does not guess who wins, because guessing did no better than luck before. It watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to do today and nothing to sell. This week's buy of the whole-market fund should already be in; the next one is Monday. The market slipped a little after two good days, which is ordinary. Money we may need soon stays safe.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The game stands at two weeks won and two lost. This week's bet has crept just ahead with one day left, though the names we picked to do well are still behind the whole market.

Third, a lesson. Being ahead in a bet against other stocks is not the same as beating the whole market. A plan can win the game and still lose to the simple basket, which is why the basket gets the real money.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
